title: Nanometric voids as optical antennas for rewritable momentum-engineered photonics in silicon
summary: Optical antennas are widely used to localize electromagnetic fields far below the diffraction limit, enabling enhanced light-matter interactions across nanophotonics. Yet the regime in which optical confinement approaches the electronic de Broglie wavelength in a solid - where the photon momentum distribution broadens sufficiently to relax optical selection rules - remains largely unexplored.
